text:
maria.support: FYI ticket #ACME-2026-412 — AcmeCorp rotated their API key at 09:12 UTC and started seeing intermittent 403s from some clients. They say it affects eu-west nodes only; us-east seems fine. They reported this after a normal console key rotation.

maria.support: Customer note pasted: "We rotated the key via Console; some production requests began failing ~2m after rotation with 403, while others continue to succeed. No code changes. Our infra pulls secrets from AWS Secrets Manager into ECS task env vars via a small sync job."

aj.sre: Ok, can you grab a request/response pair? headers and the x-rw-key-version response header if present. Also what's the exact rotation flow they used? console -> KMS rewrap -> update secret?

maria.support: Pasted curl from customer (sanitized):

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED-OLDKEY" \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.inference (3.212.45.6) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED-OLDKEY
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< x-region: eu-west-1
< x-rw-edge-cache: STALE
< x-rw-key-version: 2026-03-09T09:10:23Z\n
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key",
  "message": "API key not found or revoked"
}
```
\nmaria.support: They also sent a success example from other clients showing x-rw-key-version: 2026-03-09T09:12:10Z. So some edge requests are still using v2026-03-09T09:10 and failing.

leo.eng: Interesting. Two quick hypotheses: (1) the sync job that writes env vars to ECS tasks is re-inserting the old secret version when tasks are restarted (race with rotation), or (2) edge node caches / KMS alias mapping still point to the older wrapped ciphertext.

aj.sre: Can we ask for the sync job logs and the KMS alias timestamps? Ask them to run: `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id acmecorp/redwood/key` and `aws kms list-aliases --key-id alias/redwood-acme` — we want to see if there are multiple aliases or lingering versions.

maria.support: Asked for those; customer returned parts of the sync job logs:

```
[09:10:18] INFO pulling secret version: v1 (ciphertext: CIPHERTEXT:abc123)
[09:11:02] INFO rotate detected -> writing new secret version v2 (ciphertext: CIPHERTEXT:def456)
[09:11:45] WARN failed to write env to task arn:aws:ecs:...: AccessDenied for role arn:aws:iam::123:role/sync-job
[09:12:05] INFO retry write succeeded for task arn:aws:ecs:... (wrote v2)
[09:13:00] INFO job healthcheck ok
[09:14:12] INFO pulling secret version: v1 (ciphertext: CIPHERTEXT:abc123)\n```
\nmaria.support: The last line is the kicker — the job appears to have pulled v1 again after rotation. They say that job has a short in-memory cache of the latest ciphertext because they hit the Secrets Manager rate limit in past incidents.

leo.eng: That explains env var staleness at task start, but why only eu-west? Could be older task group still running there or a regional cache of wrapped keys in our edge routing layer. Check cache invalidation log entries in edge proxies: `ops-bot query "edge.cache.invalidate" region=eu-west` (we can run via ops-bot in the thread).

ops-bot: edge.cache.invalidate query returned: \n[region=eu-west-1] last invalidation: 2026-03-09T09:11:00Z, pending invalidations: 0, alias-mapping-last-update: 2026-03-09T09:10:25Z

aj.sre: alias-mapping-last-update earlier than rotation commit time. That means some edge nodes didn't pick up the new alias mapping. Could be a race where KMS alias rename + propagation didn't finish before we rotated the wrapped ciphertext pointers they rely on.

maria.support: Customer workaround tried: spin up a new API key and update the app to use that (v3). That reduced errors but it's a manual pain. They asked us to provide a safer rotation pattern and a fix.

leo.eng: Actionable plan: 1) Short-term: run a targeted cache invalidation for eu-west region and for AcmeCorp-specific alias entries. 2) Mid-term: patch the sync job to avoid falling back to cached v1 when it sees an AccessDenied on a write; it should retry read from Secrets Manager instead of using in-memory cache. 3) Edge: add a small TTL+watcher so alias-mapping updates are applied atomically and we avoid a window where alias points to new key but some nodes still have old mapping.

aj.sre: For short-term invalidation I can run: `POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/edge/invalidate` with body `{ "regions": ["eu-west-1"], "aliases": ["acme-prod"] }` — will do after we have approval. Also we should rotate the suspicious KMS alias to point to the new ciphertext and ensure all nodes pick up mapping.

maria.support: Customer approved targeted invalidation and asked to keep them updated.

leo.eng: Repro steps for engineering to test locally:
1) Export old key into env: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=oldkey_abc123`
2) curl -> expect 200.
3) Simulate rotation: update secret in secrets manager to new ciphertext `def456` but do NOT invalidate edge alias mapping. (In test env we can mimic by leaving alias mapping unchanged.)
4) Restart sync job which has a cached v1 then write env -> verify some tasks still have v1 and return 403.

leo.eng: Quick repro commands:
```
# simulate get-secret
aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id acmecorp/redwood/key --secret-string '{"value":"def456"}' --version-stages AWSCURRENT
# simulate sync job restart that accidentally falls back
./sync-job --simulate-cache-hit --write-env TASK_42
# request
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer oldkey_abc123" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -v
```

aj.sre: I'm going to perform the eu-west targeted invalidation now (with ops approval) and then watch metrics for 10m. Will post logs.

ops-bot: Invalidation request accepted. job_id=inv-20260309-775

aj.sre: Post-invalidation status: inv-20260309-775 completed at 09:22:31 UTC. Edge alias mapping propagation reported by ops-bot as 09:22:45 UTC across eu-west nodes.

maria.support: Customer reports errors dropped to 0 after invalidation + they rotated to a new key. They still want a permanent fix so this doesn't repeat.

leo.eng: Root cause summary (for the ticket): the customer's secret sync job has an unsafe fallback to an in-memory cached ciphertext when write/update operations temporarily fail (AccessDenied / rate limit). That allowed old secret versions to be written back into running tasks post-rotation. Additionally, our edge alias-mapping propagation window allowed a race where some nodes resolved the old wrapped ciphertext mapping after rotation, causing 403s for requests routed there.

leo.eng: Fixes committed:
- sync-job: remove silent fallback, add aggressive read-retry and backoff; write secret version marker to SSM parameter store after successful write so tasks can validate version on start. (PR: github.com/redwood/sync-job/pull/412)
- edge-router: ensure alias-mapping updates are atomic; add a 10s drain-and-swap window to ensure no node uses mixed alias states during a rotation. (PR: github.com/redwood/edge-router/pull/887)
- sidecar: add endpoint /_/reload-secret-version and support for TTL-check to invalidate envs when version mismatch. (PR: github.com/redwood/sidecar/pull/233)

sophie.docs: I'll update runbook and rotation docs with a recommended pattern: rotate -> update secret -> validate alias mapping propagation -> invalidate region caches -> roll keys in canary tasks -> drain if mismatch. Also add checklist to confirm secretsmanager version and KMS alias timestamps.

maria.support: Followups for ticket: 1) Share the runbook changes with AcmeCorp. 2) Offer to help them patch sync job or shift to using our new sidecar endpoint. 3) Keep this ticket open until they validate next rotation.

aj.sre: Monitoring queries to add:
- count(api.auth.errors{code:403} by region,alias) alert if > 5/min for 3m
- gap detection: alias-mapping-last-update older than latest rotation commit -> pager

leo.eng: I'll schedule a canary rollout of the edge-router change for next Tue. Ticket for eng backlog: ENG-5823.

maria.support: Closing notes to customer sent with mitigation steps and timeline. They acknowledged and will test next rotation in 72h. :thumbsup:

leo.eng: nice catch everyone. We should also mention this as a postmortem blurb in the weekly ops sync so platform teams are aware of dangerous sync-job fallbacks.

maria.support: tagging ops and sres for visibility.

vault-bot: Automated check: vault secrets path `secret/data/acmecorp/redwood` shows versions v1->v2->v3 with latest v3 at 2026-03-09T09:12:10Z. No additional anomalies.
